newsitem.title: USA: Connectics says ConXn Phase II positive.
newsitem.headline: Connectics says ConXn Phase II positive.

text.p: Connetics Corp Thursday said Phase II trial data suggest ConXn may be an effective treatment for scleroderma, a connective tissue disorder for which there is currently no treatment.
"This represents the first controlled clinical study to show positive results in the treatment of scleroderma," the company said in a statement.
The company said the test involved 64 patients, one group of which received either 25 grams per kilogram or 100 grams per kilogram per day of the drug and another group receiving placebo.

In the group receiving the lower drug dose, statistical significance was found in skin score improvement, the primary clinical endpoint, and positive trends were seen in all other parameters, the company said.
But the higher dose had no effect on the treatment group compared to placebo, as suggested by previous studies, the company said.
"Based on these data, we are committed to the continued development of ConXn for scleroderma," said Scott Harkonen, Connetics senior vice president of product development.
The Phase II data have been submitted for presentation at the American Academy of Rheumatology Annual Meeting in November, the company said.

Scleroderma is a serious connective tissue disease resulting from an excessive production of collagen, affecting 300,000 patients in the U.S., 80 percent of whom are women, Connetics added. (( New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
